entries.title: Provider-failure budget mismatch: frozen supplemental 3 vs runtime HOUR_1 ceiling 8
entries.evidence: The W12 freeze records providerFailures=3 and consecutiveFailures=3 for HOUR_1, while the live engine policy records providerFailures=8 and consecutiveFailures=6; W12's broad receipt observed 8 provider failures and its scoped receipts stopped after 6 consecutive failures, proving the engine values were the ones applied.
entries.whyItMatters: A declared experiment envelope that disagrees with the enforced runtime ceiling makes the frozen budget untrustworthy and can silently change stopping behaviour between waves.
entries.nextAction: Closed: engine policy is the sole authority, declared envelopes are derived and validated field-by-field, the historical 3/3 values are a permanent negative probe, and D-139 succeeds D-138 without rewriting it.

entries.title: gate:local SYNTHETIC_CAMPAIGN timeout classification (receipt sha256:c5107a12b6bd0a89263c5c2)
entries.evidence: W12 `gate:local` passed nine groups and timed out in the serial synthetic lane at its 600 s MEDIUM bound; the direct lane passed 1,897/1,897 afterwards on the same tree.
entries.whyItMatters: An unclassified gate timeout is an equivocal validation lane; Phase A must resolve it to exactly one measured cause before closure, without raising the bound.
entries.nextAction: Re-run the direct and gate-dispatched lanes back-to-back on an idle host with uptime/process snapshots, diff the synthetic manifest file count against the base SHA, and classify as exactly one of the six causes; reclassify to LOCAL_FIX_REQUIRED and mark blocking if the cause is REAL_GATE_TIMEOUT_DEFECT or DUPLICATE_WORK.

entries.title: Provider failure classification is a two-value taxonomy (REASONER_TIMEOUT, REASONER_NONZERO_EXIT)
entries.evidence: W12 receipts can only name REASONER_TIMEOUT and REASONER_NONZERO_EXIT, so absence, probe timeout, invalid structured response, quota/namespace unavailability, auth failure, and local CLI failure are indistinguishable.
entries.whyItMatters: W13 failover eligibility depends on the failure class; an incomplete taxonomy would make transitions either unsafe or impossible to justify.
entries.nextAction: Implement the ten-member provider taxonomy with sanitized retention (exit code, duration, byte counts only), and cover each classified transition plus the unknown fallback with regressions.

entries.title: Per-provider attribution absent from predecessor receipts (providerRetries NOT_CAPTURED)
entries.evidence: W12 receipts carry a single provider field, `providerRetries: "NOT_CAPTURED"`, and no per-provider call/failure/byte/transition breakdown.
entries.whyItMatters: A multi-provider W13 run cannot report per-provider attribution unless the receipt schema captures it; merging providers would hide which provider failed and why.
entries.nextAction: Define and regress the W13 run-receipt schema with per-provider calls, valid responses, failures by class, retries, bytes, wall time, and transitions; machine-capture every field.

entries.title: Current-source census is truthfully TRUNCATED at the Ouchan enumeration bound
entries.evidence: The W12 census admitted 4,124 files but recorded `sourceInventory.completeness: TRUNCATED` because Ouchan exceeded its enumeration bound, so the headline count is a floor, not a population.
entries.whyItMatters: Any W13 denominator derived from a truncated population must be reported as a floor and never as an exhaustive count.
entries.nextAction: Determine whether the enumeration bound can be safely raised or paginated within the existing resource contract; if yes implement and re-run the census; if no add a mechanical check that every metric consuming the inventory treats TRUNCATED as a floor, reusing truncation-truth-discovery-paging vocabulary, with a regression.

entries.title: Aggregate measurement completeness is not schema-guaranteed
entries.evidence: W12's aggregate is a task artifact without a required-metric schema or a check that every required metric is machine-derived; several fields are simply absent and only some are marked NOT_CAPTURED.
entries.whyItMatters: A required metric that is silently absent can inflate or erase a denominator without any validator noticing.
entries.nextAction: Cross-check the required global-metric list against the aggregation schema; wire real machine capture or add explicit NOT_CAPTURED fields with reasons; regress that no required metric is silently absent.

entries.title: Candidate/admission invariant is not proven by a mechanical negative probe
entries.evidence: No fixture proves that a record declaring `admitted: true` with no reproduction receipt, evidence reference, or dossier identity is rejected by aggregation; the invariant held only because such a record did not occur.
entries.whyItMatters: An aggregation that trusts a self-declared admission flag would let model text mint an admission.
entries.nextAction: Add a fixture-based negative probe that aggregation fails closed on an inconsistent admission record, and wire the validation into the aggregation path.

entries.title: No regression proves a failed provider call mints no investigation progress
entries.evidence: W12 scoped receipts show zero source actions after six provider failures, but no regression asserts that a failed provider call cannot mint a source action, inspected target, hypothesis, candidate, admission, or dossier, nor that repeated failure yields a provider-blocked result rather than a valid zero-yield result.
entries.whyItMatters: Provider failure must remain categorically distinct from a valid zero-yield measurement.
entries.nextAction: Add the failed-provider fake-progress regression over the existing runtime path with a fake failing provider.

entries.title: Production Completion Group 12 items 12.7, 12.8, 12.11, 12.12 still annotate W12's blocked state
entries.evidence: All four unchecked items name W12 PARTIAL — BLOCKED as their current annotation; their checkbox state and text have not been reconciled with W13's activated state.
entries.whyItMatters: The programme's ledger must not present a superseded blocked state as current once W13 is active.
entries.nextAction: Re-annotate the four items as far as Phase A evidence truthfully supports, preserving predecessor text, and reconcile again against actual W13 evidence at Phase B close.

entries.title: Parent programme JSON is stale (currentWave W12, exactNextAction 'Resume W12...')
entries.evidence: currentWave is W12, YIELD_W12.status is 'blocked', and exactNextAction/resumeRecipe still instruct resuming W12, which is COMPLETE with verdict PARTIAL — BLOCKED.
entries.whyItMatters: A stale programme pointer routes a fresh session to the wrong task and misstates W12's status.
entries.nextAction: Update currentWave, exactNextAction, resumeRecipe, and YIELD_W12 status (preserving the blocked verdict) to route W13.

entries.title: Governed current-state and README yield figures not reconciled with W13
entries.evidence: The W13 live-state binding and a W13 status row were added at activation; published yield figures remain W12's and the W13 outcome is not yet measured.
entries.whyItMatters: Governed surfaces must agree with receipts after Phase B closes.
entries.nextAction: Reconcile README/current-state yield figures from actual W13 receipts at Phase B close.

entries.title: Predecessor single-provider validity and never-probe-later-candidates rules conflict with the W13 failover policy
entries.evidence: The archived W12 requirement freezes one provider for the whole wave and forbids probing later candidates; W13's delta replaces it with policy-governed deterministic failover, and the W12 selection policy artifact still states the old rule.
entries.whyItMatters: Phase B must run under exactly one declared validity rule; leaving two live rules would make the wave's result ambiguous.
entries.nextAction: Freeze the W13 provider-resilience policy and evaluation freeze that bind the failover rule, and record in the W13 evidence that W12's artifacts remain immutable predecessor history rather than live authority; change no admission, reproduction, leakage, or novelty requirement.

entries.title: Environment/host-capability lanes outside the frozen owner scope
entries.evidence: DEV/NEXT/production contact, authenticated Alphaus runtime, browser product journeys, database/data-plane, cloud/infrastructure, external publication, Slack/Leslie/Pondr/Notion, and issue/PR creation remain NOT AUTHORIZED for W13.
entries.whyItMatters: These lanes are deliberately unavailable and must not be reopened by an experiment fix.
entries.nextAction: None in W13; a future owner authorization is required to revisit any of these lanes.
